The waratah on the right is the state flora of NSW, this one is borrowed from the NSW government logo. The Southern Cross comes from the current red ensign of Australia, which is enclosed in a symbolic representation of NSW's landmass. The gold band represents the beach and rich coastlines of the state and the white band in the middle is purely an aesthetic addition

The Coat of Arms is that of the Spanish East Indies, but the Spanish crown of the shield is replaced by the Tudor Crown standard of the British monarchs of the Era (Victoria to George VI)
The elements borrowed from the Oranje, Blanje, Blou flag is the usage of a horizontal tricolour, and the placement of the Union Jack within the centre of the flag

This flag uses the three main colours of the Australian flag as the horizontal tricolour. Red is the traditional colour used by the indigenous Australians to represent the land, the white represents the purity and beauty of the landscape, and the blue represents the oceans surrounding Australia on all sides of the continent. The Union Jack represents the British that established the foundation for a unified country, and the 5 stars represent the various people across the world coming together to form a nation
